summary: The woman in the Song calls herself a flower of Sharon and a lily of the valleys. Isaiah evokes the same flower when he pictures the desert bursting into bloom.

senses.definition: A flowering plant associated with the plain of Sharon and used as an image of the desert in bloom.

evidence.note: The speaker pairs her flower of Sharon with a lily of the valleys. The answering voice takes up the lily image in the next verse.
The desert rejoices and blossoms like this plant. The following verse continues the picture of abundant bloom.

cognates.gloss: flower in the Syriac rendering of Isaiah

evidence.locator: Ḫ, p. 8, ḫabaṣillatu, reed shoot sense

note: Neither passage describes the flower closely enough to choose between crocus, narcissus and other proposed identifications. The Syriac form in Isaiah may reflect the Hebrew it translates. The Akkadian term names a reed shoot and its initial consonant makes the historical connection uncertain.
